title: Square wand, round bubble. And where do the colors come from? | So That's Why
description:
Little Q bent some wire into a square wand and blew bubbles, but they still came out round. The bubble soap is completely clear, yet the colors on the bubble kept swirling, until the top turned black and it popped. How can one thin film be in charge of both the shape and the colors?

In this episode, the Chief and Little Q follow one square wand and one bottle of bubble soap: first they use a balloon's skin as a comparison to see how the bubble film keeps trying to shrink, and why a bubble floating in the air gets pulled round; then they let two and three bubbles stick together to test that idea: when they're the same size, the wall between them is flat, and when one is big and one is small, the small one actually pushes into the big one. Next comes the question of color: light bounces back once from the outside of the film and once from the inside, like two rings of ripples meeting in a pond, so some colors get stronger and others cancel out; and finally, with the same bubble, they work out whether a color is changing with time or with where your eyes are.

The illustrations in this episode were made with AI; they are diagrams, not photos of bubbles. The numbers are approximate. You can't measure exactly how thick a bubble film is just from the colors in a photo. The source of every claim is listed in the references below.
